chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar and Hafsh ibn al-Bakhtari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"It is appropriate for the pilgrim, when he has completed his ritual duties and intends to depart, to purchase dates with a dirham and give them in charity, so that it serves as expiation for any minor defects that entered upon him during his Hajj, such as shaving [hair] or the falling of lice, or similar matters."
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended charity for expiating minor defects after Hajj?
ai.summary: In the *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes a specific, accessible form of expiation for minor ritual impediments (*hukm*) like shaving or lice, emphasizing ease for the pilgrim. This practice reflects the Shia juristic principle of balancing ritual purity with practical mercy, ensuring that minor oversights do not burden the pilgrim excessively. It highlights the importance of concluding Hajj with acts of charity to spiritually cleanse any residual imperfections from the sacred rites.
